rows.source: HSE home-working health and safety guidance
rows.verified: Employers have the same health and safety responsibilities for home workers as for workers based at the employer's workplace.

rows.source: HSE home-working health and safety guidance
rows.verified: An employer's risk assessment must cover home workers.

rows.source: HSE home-working health and safety guidance
rows.verified: A proportionate assessment will often not require a home visit, although visits may be appropriate for special needs or significant hazards.

rows.source: HSE home-working health and safety guidance
rows.verified: Assessment should consider communication, the type and duration of work, how it can be done safely and any controls required.

rows.source: HSE home-working health and safety guidance
rows.verified: Advice, self-assessment tools, questionnaires and phone or video discussions can be used to assess and manage home-working risks.

rows.source: HSE home-working health and safety guidance
rows.verified: Alternative workplace arrangements should be agreed where the home environment is unsuitable and reasonably practicable controls cannot protect the worker.

rows.source: HSE home-working health and safety guidance
rows.verified: Stress risk assessment duties apply equally to home workers, who may require additional support and maintained social contact.

rows.source: HSE home-working health and safety guidance
rows.verified: Employers should discuss workloads, encourage breaks and leave and avoid unrealistic deadlines or expectations of out-of-hours responses.

rows.source: HSE home-working health and safety guidance
rows.verified: Home-working risk depends on the task, duration, equipment, workstation, domestic environment, isolation, communication, disability needs and ability to implement controls.

rows.source: HSE home-working health and safety guidance
rows.verified: General risk assessment, communication, DSE, work environment, stress and alternative arrangements guidance does not prove the current condition, exposure or control performance at an individual parcel and does not establish an exact event or illness probability.

rows.source: HSE pregnant-worker and new-mother protection guidance
rows.verified: Once notified in writing, an employer must complete an individual risk assessment for a pregnant worker or new mother.

rows.source: HSE pregnant-worker and new-mother protection guidance
rows.verified: The individual assessment applies to workers who are pregnant, gave birth in the previous six months or are breastfeeding.

rows.source: HSE pregnant-worker and new-mother protection guidance
rows.verified: Identified risks to the worker or child must be reduced, removed or controlled and the worker informed of the safety measures.

rows.source: HSE pregnant-worker and new-mother protection guidance
rows.verified: Common issues can include prolonged sitting or standing, heavy loads, long hours, stress, temperature, noise and workstation posture.

rows.source: HSE pregnant-worker and new-mother protection guidance
rows.verified: If a significant risk cannot be controlled, working conditions or hours should first be adjusted.

rows.source: HSE pregnant-worker and new-mother protection guidance
rows.verified: If adjustment is not possible, suitable alternative work should be offered on the same terms and conditions, including pay.

rows.source: HSE pregnant-worker and new-mother protection guidance
rows.verified: If suitable alternative work is not possible, the worker must be suspended on full pay for as long as necessary for protection.

rows.source: HSE pregnant-worker and new-mother protection guidance
rows.verified: The individual assessment must be reviewed as pregnancy progresses or work changes, and risky night work may require suitable alternative day work.

rows.source: HSE pregnant-worker and new-mother protection guidance
rows.verified: Pregnancy and new-mother risk depends on pregnancy stage, medical advice, task, posture, hours, substances, temperature, noise, infection, work changes and individual condition.

rows.source: HSE pregnant-worker and new-mother protection guidance
rows.verified: General individual risk assessment, controls, alternative work, suspension, review and night work guidance does not prove the current condition, exposure or control performance at an individual parcel and does not establish an exact event or illness probability.
